entries.text: Hello, everyone. Well done on the midterm exam.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_01

entries.text: Some of you earned perfect scores, and others\nseemed to have a bit of trouble, but I can tell\r\nthat you all tried your best.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_02

entries.text: I am quite pleased to say that every last one of\nyou passed.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_03

entries.text: I can only assume that this means you have all\ncome to love numbers![VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_04

entries.text: Stay sharp, and try your best for the rest of my\nclasses, too![VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_05

entries.text: Speaking of staying “sharp,” do you know how\nthat word applies to Pokémon battles?\r\nThat’s right—it has to do with stat boosts![VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_06

entries.text: A Pokémon’s stats can rise and fall throughout\nthe course of battle, correct?[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_07

entries.text: For example, if a Pokémon uses the move\nWork Up, its Attack and Sp. Atk stats will rise by\r\none stage each.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_08

entries.text: And, as you may know, each time a Pokémon’s\nAttack or Sp. Atk rises one stage, moves affected\r\nby that stat will deal 50 percent more damage.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_09

entries.text:
If that same Pokémon from our previous example
were to use Work Up again, both its Attack and
Sp. Atk will have risen by two stages total.\c
This results in a 100 percent increase to damage
dealt, making its moves twice as strong![VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_10

entries.text: Swords Dance, on the other hand, boosts Attack\nby two stages at once, allowing the Pokémon to\r\ndeal double damage after just a single use![VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_11

entries.text: Using Swords Dance twice would boost the\nPokémon’s Attack stat by four stages. How much\r\nmore damage, then, would this Pokémon deal?[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_12

entries.text: Double damage
entries.label: class_b_05_select_01

entries.text: Triple damage
entries.label: class_b_05_select_02

entries.text: Quadruple damage
entries.label: class_b_05_select_03

entries.text: Ah, yes. This question is a tricky one, isn’t it?\c\nDamage would be doubled if it’d used Work Up\ntwice, but we’re talking about Swords Dance.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_answer_01

entries.text: Wow, that’s great! You answered this difficult\nquestion with ease, [VAR 0x0100(0000)]![VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_answer_02

entries.text: Ah, yes. This question is a tricky one, isn’t it?\c\nJust because it boosts the Pokémon’s stat by four\nstages doesn’t mean damage is quadrupled.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_answer_03

entries.text: Each stage that a Pokémon’s Attack or Sp. Atk\nstat is raised increases its damage by 50 percent.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_13

entries.text: So, being raised four stages would result in a four\ntimes 50 percent—or 200 percent—increase.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_14

entries.text: The base damage of a move is 100 percent, so\nadding 200 percent to that gives us 300 percent.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_15

entries.text: In other words, the next move the Pokémon uses\nwill deal triple damage.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_16

entries.text: Type matchups, critical-hit damage, and other\nfactors all play into these calculations as well,\r\nso even a small boost must be taken seriously.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_17

entries.text:
By the way, if a stat simply “rose,” that means it
has gone up by one stage.\c
If it “rose sharply,” that’s two stages.\c
And if it “rose drastically,” that’s three stages.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_18

entries.text: Just so you know, the X Attack and X Sp. Atk\nitems, which can only be used in battle, can be\r\nused to sharply boost those respective stats.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_19

entries.text: Oh, my. Is that the bell? I suppose that’s all for\nnow. What a shame...[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_20

entries.text: Today’s lesson was a little difficult, so be sure to\nreview what you learned in order to stay “sharp”!\r\nI’ll see you all again next class.[VAR 0x0114(0025)]
entries.label: class_b_05_math_21
